parameters.content:
## Flight-Finder (Google Flights link builder)

**Flow:** Gmail Trigger (all inbox mail) → Prep Requests (keyword-filtered to real flight requests) → Build Gemini Request → Gemini (extracts trip details) → Parse & Build Flights Link → [Ready? IF] →
  • ready: Gmail Reply with the Google Flights link + trip summary
  • needs_clarification: Gmail Reply asking for the missing detail
Both branches also post to Slack for visibility, then continue to Gmail: Mark Processed.

**Why a link instead of a live price API:** Google Flights has no public API, and paid flight APIs (Kiwi Tequila, Amadeus, Skyscanner) need approved keys and often per-request cost. This builds a pre-filled Google Flights search URL using its natural-language `q=` parameter — free, no key, and shows real live prices the moment it's opened.

**IMPORTANT — execution modes:** `Build Gemini Request` and `Parse & Build Flights Link` are set to "Run Once for Each Item". `Prep Requests` uses the default "Run Once for All Items".

**Before activating:**
1. Credentials: Gmail (trigger + reply + label), Gemini (PaLM) API, Slack.
2. `Prep Requests`: set EXEC_EMAIL; adjust SUBJECT_KEYWORDS if requests use different phrasing.
3. `Parse & Build Flights Link`: set DEFAULT_ORIGIN to your usual home city (used when a requester doesn't state where they're flying from) and EXEC_NAME.
4. `Gmail: Reply (Ready)` and `Gmail: Reply (Clarify)`: these use the Reply operation — the exact field names may need reselecting after import (this is the least-tested part of the workflow).
5. `Gmail: Mark Processed`: pick a real label.
6. `Slack: Notify`: confirm channel.

**IMPORTANT when reimporting after any future fix:** select all nodes (Ctrl+A) and delete them BEFORE importing the new file, or n8n will auto-rename nodes with a trailing "1" and break every cross-node reference in the code.
